sn5.1:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.
sn5.1:1.3: Then the nun Āḷavikā, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up her bowl and robe, was entering Sāvatthī for alms.
sn5.1:1.4: After walking for alms in Sāvatthī, and returning from the alms-round after the meal, she approached the Blind Man’s Wood seeking for seclusion.
sn5.1:1.5: Then the Wicked Māra desiring to give rise to fear, terror, and horror in the nun Āḷavikā, desiring to drive her out of seclusion, approached the nun Āḷavikā, and after approaching he addressed the nun Āḷavikā with a verse:
sn5.1:2.1: “There is no escape from the world,
sn5.1:2.2: why do you try with seclusion?
sn5.1:3.1: Then it occurred to the nun Āḷavikā:
sn5.1:3.2: “Who is this, a human or a non-human, speaking this verse?”
sn5.1:3.3: Then it occurred to the nun Āḷavikā:
sn5.1:3.4: “This is the Wicked Māra desiring to give rise to fear, terror, and horror in me, desiring to drive me out of seclusion, who speaks this verse.”
sn5.1:3.5: Then the nun Āḷavikā having understood: This is the Wicked Māra, replied with this verse to the Wicked Māra:
sn5.1:4.1: “There is an escape from the world,
sn5.1:4.2: which I have attained through wisdom,
sn5.1:4.3: You do not know that state, you Wicked one, kin of the heedless,
sn5.1:5.1: Sensual pleasures are like an axe,
sn5.1:5.3: That which you say is sensual delight,
sn5.1:5.4: in that for me there is no delight.”
sn5.1:6.1: Then the Wicked Māra (thought): “The nun Āḷavikā knows me!” and pained and depressed he vanished right there.
